solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Dog chasing black bird (6)

indicators.note: the bird runs along behind the black, so EAGLE comes after B

annotation.surface: A dog running after a dark bird.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'chasing' as the dog's action, but it only places the bird behind the black. 'Dog' is the definition, not the chaser.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the beagle is one small, floppy-eared breed of hunting hound, kept by packs for hare-coursing.

entries.clue: Cow’s lick below forehead (8)

indicators.note: in a down answer, what is below comes second, so BEAT follows BROW

blocks.note: to lick an opponent is to beat them

annotation.surface: A cow's lick: the tuft of hair sticking up over someone's forehead.
annotation.walkthrough: A cowlick is a stubborn tuft of hair, which is the picture; but 'Cow' is a verb meaning intimidate, and ’s is 'is'.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both verbs mean intimidating someone with threats or stern looks until they give in.

entries.clue: Terrible entertainment briefly interrupts boring item (5)

indicators.note: cut short: FUN loses its last letter
breaks into the middle of AWL

blocks.note: an awl is a tool for boring holes

annotation.surface: Some dreadful show cuts in on a dull item.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Boring' pretends to mean dull; it means making holes, which is what an awl does.
annotation.definitionFit: Awful and terrible both mean very bad.

entries.clue: Have friend over for drink (3)

indicators.note: turned over: PAL written backwards in a down answer

blocks.note: a pal is a friend; 'Have' just sets up the phrase 'have over'

annotation.surface: An invitation to a friend to come round for a drink.
annotation.walkthrough: To have a friend over is to host them; in the wordplay 'over' turns PAL upside down.
annotation.definitionFit: A synonym by manner: cats and dogs take up liquid with quick flicks of the tongue, and that is lapping.

entries.clue: Most amusing peer recalled in case (8)

indicators.note: called back: LORD reads backwards

blocks.note: lest = in case, as in 'lest we forget'

annotation.surface: A comic lord brought back to appear in a court case.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In case' looks like a container instruction, but it is one unit, the old conjunction meaning 'for fear that'.
annotation.definitionFit: Droll means wryly amusing; drollest is the most so.

entries.clue: Event where competitors use craft? (7)

blocks.note: a contest of some kind, which the surface suggests is won by skill
craft here means boats, not guile; the question mark flags the second sense

annotation.surface: A contest won by cunning.
annotation.walkthrough: Craft reads as skill or cunning; here it is boats, plural like 'aircraft'.
annotation.definitionFit: The answer names a meeting of rowing or sailing races, so every competitor really does use a craft.

entries.clue: Tricky deception shocked Nigel? Dear me (11)

indicators.note: the letters are jolted into a new order

annotation.surface: Someone is dismayed that Nigel has been taken in by a trick.
annotation.walkthrough: The punctuation makes 'Dear me' an exclamation, but it is simply fodder alongside NIGEL.
annotation.definitionFit: Legerdemain is sleight of hand, and so trickery or deception.

entries.clue: Pen accompaniment to letter (9)

blocks.note: a fenced area where sheep or pigs are kept
a document tucked into the envelope alongside a letter

annotation.surface: Writing a letter with a pen.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface makes 'Pen' a writing tool, which sits nicely with 'letter'; it is an animal pen.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: a fenced area for livestock, and any document posted inside the same envelope, marked 'enc.' at the foot of business mail.

entries.clue: Tense argument leads to engineer lobbing tool (6)

indicators.note: the leading letters of the next two words

blocks.note: a row is an argument (rhymes with 'cow')
first letters of engineer and lobbing

annotation.surface: A heated quarrel ends with an engineer throwing a tool.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Tense' looks like an adjective describing the argument; it is the abbreviation T.
annotation.definitionFit: A trowel is a small hand tool for gardening or plastering.

entries.clue: Shabby-looking husband boards small boat (6)

indicators.note: gets on board, so H goes inside DINGY

annotation.surface: A scruffy husband climbs into a little boat.
annotation.walkthrough: Only one letter separates DINGY from DINGHY; the husband supplies it.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the open rowing or sailing tender carried by yachts, or raced on lakes, is the classic little boat.

entries.clue: High season issue (9)

annotation.surface: A problem arising during the busiest time of year.
annotation.walkthrough: 'High season' is a single holiday phrase, and 'issue' looks like a problem; it means children, as in 'died without issue'.
annotation.definitionFit: Issue is a legal and formal word for offspring.

entries.clue: Reptile beginning to generate reverberation, from the sound of it (5)

indicators.note: the first letter of generate
ECHO is said, and spelt as it sounds

annotation.surface: A lizard first makes a noise that bounces back.
annotation.walkthrough: The homophone only applies to the echo, which is why the spelling ECKO can join a plain G.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: this small wall-climbing lizard with sticky toe pads is one kind of reptile.

entries.clue: He campaigns against nonsense and expects to make a killing (11)

definitions.note: the definition shares its subject 'He' with the wordplay: he who expects to make a killing

indicators.note: placed up against: BULL sits beside FIGHTER

blocks.note: one who campaigns is a fighter

annotation.surface: A political campaigner against nonsense who hopes to profit handsomely.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Make a killing' is the idiom for making a lot of money, which fits the campaigner; literally, a bullfighter kills the bull.
annotation.definitionFit: A matador enters the ring expecting to kill the bull.

entries.clue: Tender cut of ling I’m often cooking (5,6)

indicators.note: the letters are cooked up into a new arrangement

annotation.surface: A cook says a tender cut of ling is often on the menu.
annotation.walkthrough: Ling is a fish, so 'Tender cut of ling' reads as one phrase; the definition ends at 'cut'.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: this French name covers small steaks taken from the narrow end of the beef tenderloin, prized for softness.

entries.clue: Broadcast outstanding work of poetry (3)

indicators.note: put out over the air, so heard rather than seen

annotation.surface: Radio airs a brilliant poem.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Outstanding' pretends to praise the poem; it means unpaid.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Keats and Horace wrote this formal lyric kind of poem, often addressed to its subject.

entries.clue: Some royal PR I agree brought about radio exposure (7)

indicators.note: part of the following words
turned about, so read backwards

blocks.note: the run of letters inside roYAL PR I Agree

annotation.surface: A royal publicist agrees that a spot of media attention would help.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is about press management, which hides the backwards run of letters in plain sight.
annotation.definitionFit: Airplay is the time a record or item gets on radio.

entries.clue: Bardot endlessly tossed hair; that’ll stop the traffic! (9)

indicators.note: BARDOT loses its last letter
the remaining letters are thrown into a new order

blocks.note: a lock is a strand of hair

annotation.surface: Brigitte Bardot flicks her hair and stops traffic, as a beauty does.
annotation.walkthrough: Brigitte Bardot was a French film star; a head-turner 'stops the traffic', and a roadblock does so literally.
annotation.definitionFit: Police or soldiers set up a barrier across a road to halt vehicles, so it literally stops cars, while a beauty only figuratively does.

entries.clue: Trees usually shade this ace location (6)

blocks.note: A = ace, as on playing cards
the place where an event is held

annotation.surface: A pleasant spot where trees give shade.
annotation.walkthrough: An avenue is traditionally a road lined with trees, which is why the definition is fair.
annotation.definitionFit: An avenue is a tree-lined road, so trees usually shade it.

entries.clue: Place for putting every other sample of early plants? (8)

indicators.note: take every other letter of early: E, R, Y

annotation.surface: A spot for planting out seedlings.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Putting' sounds like putting things down; it is the golf stroke, and the green is where it happens.
annotation.definitionFit: A collective noun: leaves and growing vegetation taken together, as in decorating a room with fresh foliage.

entries.clue: Femme fatale forgetting ultimate sacred word (6)

indicators.note: ultimate means last, and forgetting it means the word is written without its final letter

annotation.surface: A seductress forgets the last holy word.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Femme fatale' suggests a name like Mata Hari; it is a mantrap, a woman who ensnares men.
annotation.definitionFit: A mantra is a sacred word or sound repeated in meditation.

entries.clue: Jar American artist filled with noodle soup (7)

indicators.note: a jar filled with soup holds it inside, so the soup's letters go within the American artist

blocks.note: pho is a Vietnamese noodle soup

annotation.surface: An American painter's jar of noodle soup.
annotation.walkthrough: The artist is a Royal Academician, the standard crossword artist, and 'American artist' is split into two abbreviations that sit either side of the soup.
annotation.definitionFit: An amphora is a tall ancient jar with two handles.

entries.clue: Lay rug in a street in Paris to the west (7)

indicators.note: a rug laid in a street sits within it, so the rug's letters go inside the a-plus-street pair
running leftwards in an across answer, so RUE reads backwards

blocks.note: a mat is a small rug

blocks.clueFragment: street in Paris to the west
blocks.note: rue is French for street, reversed

annotation.surface: Instructions to put down a carpet in a Parisian street.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Lay' reads as a verb telling you to put the rug down; it is the adjective, as in lay person.
annotation.definitionFit: Lay means non-professional, which is what an amateur is.

entries.clue: Getting older, each caged dingo freed from captivity (6)

indicators.note: each word loses the outer letters that cage it

annotation.surface: Every captive dingo, now old, is released.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Caged' seems to describe the dingo; it is a second word to be stripped, and 'each' says to do both.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the present participle describes something advancing in years, like an elderly population or a maturing wine.

entries.clue: Ecstasy and booze upset mother — it’s a complex problem (6)

indicators.note: turned upside down in a down answer, so GIN reads upwards

annotation.surface: Drugs, drink and an upset mother make for a tangled family problem.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Upset mother' reads as one phrase; 'upset' belongs to the booze.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a riddle or mystery that resists solving, as Churchill called Russia 'a riddle wrapped in a mystery inside an enigma'.

entries.clue: Nick has suspension reversed (3)

indicators.note: a reversed decision is overturned, and the same word tells you to turn the letters round

annotation.surface: A player called Nick has his ban overturned on appeal.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Nick' is dressed as a name; it is the verb, to nick or steal.
annotation.definitionFit: To nab and to nick both mean to steal or to arrest.

entries.clue: Repel big man, somehow withstanding all attacks (11)

indicators.note: in some way or other: rearrange the letters

annotation.surface: Fending off a large attacker while staying unbeaten.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Repel' sits naturally with 'attacks', so it looks like part of the definition; it is fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: Impregnable means unable to be captured or broken into.

entries.clue: Northern child I must shelter in farm building (5)

indicators.note: I takes cover inside BARN

blocks.note: a barn is a farm building

annotation.surface: A child in the north has to take shelter in a barn.
annotation.walkthrough: Bairn is the Scottish and northern English word for a child, which is why 'Northern' is in the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Bairn is the word for a child in Scotland and northern England.

entries.clue: Adult expressed hint of exasperation (5)

indicators.note: put into speech, so heard rather than spelt

blocks.note: a grown person is an adult

annotation.surface: A grown-up lets slip a little sign of irritation.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Adult' looks like the person doing the expressing; it is the word to be spoken.
annotation.definitionFit: The low moaning noise people make when irritated or fed up gives away their feelings, so it is a small sign of them.

entries.clue: After work, I phone Leo — he loves a good whine on the blower (9)

definitions.text: he loves a good whine on the blower

indicators.note: once worked over, the letters are rearranged

annotation.surface: After work I ring Leo, who loves a good moan on the phone.
annotation.walkthrough: 'The blower' is British slang for the phone; the definition is a pun, since whine sounds like wine.
annotation.definitionFit: From Greek oinos, wine, plus -phile, lover: a wine connoisseur, and whine on the phone sounds the same.

entries.clue: Boxer dog with a flat, wrinkled face (3)

definitions.text: dog with a flat, wrinkled face

blocks.note: a prizefighter; the slang is short for pugilist

blocks.clueFragment: dog with a flat, wrinkled face
blocks.note: a small toy breed with a snub nose and curled tail

annotation.surface: A boxer dog with a squashed, creased face.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface makes Boxer the dog breed; it is a fighter, and the dog is the second definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A pug is a boxer (pugilist) and a small flat-faced dog.

entries.clue: State vessel evacuated American elite troops (8)

indicators.note: emptied of its middle, leaving the outer letters

blocks.note: the SAS is the British Special Air Service

annotation.surface: A state ship is cleared of American special forces.
annotation.walkthrough: 'State vessel' reads as a ship of state; 'State' is the definition, and the American is emptied, not the ship.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: one of the fifty American states, in the south, with Little Rock as its capital.

entries.clue: Copenhagen cybersex hosting business (6)

indicators.note: the words play host to the answer

annotation.surface: A Danish company that runs online sex services.
annotation.walkthrough: The racy surface is a distraction; the answer spans the two words.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: travel, advertising and employment firms are all this kind of company acting for clients.
